title: Coherent coefficient comparisons for rational compact-support exchange
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A coefficient stage is a finite intermediate field of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
be a compact-support square with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its pulled-back compactification $c'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Assume the scheme and integral-operation hypotheses of [thm-cbc-finite-extension] at every coefficient stage: the four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional, $\ell$ is invertible on them, and $f$ is separated of finite type; $g$ is arbitrary. For each $W=X,Y,X',Y'$, work with the completed integral category $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{int}}_E(W)=\Dbc(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E(W)=\Dbc(W,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $(j_f,p_f)=(j,p)$ and $(j_{f'},p_{f'})=(j',p')$. For $h=f,f'$, put $H_{h,E}=Rh_{!,E}=Rp_{h,*,E}j_{h,!}$, the rational extensions [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] of the completed-coefficient compactification operations [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. For $u=g,g'$, write $P_{u,E}=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], extended to the raw rational categories. Write $T^W_{L/E}$, $a^W_{N,L,E}$ and $\sigma^W_{L/E}$ for the scalar extensions, associators and shift comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

For every inclusion $E\subseteq L$ of coefficient stages, there are specified exact natural isomorphisms
$$b^h_{L/E}:T^{\operatorname{target}(h)}_{L/E}H_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{h,L}T^{\operatorname{source}(h)}_{L/E}\qquad(h=f,f')$$
given by the proper direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] and the derived coefficient-change version of the localized ringed-site extension-by-zero tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. All equations below hold for every object $K$ in the source category of the displayed functors. They are comparisons between the stated raw PBC categories. They are identity for $L=E$, commute with the specified shifts, and for $E\subset L\subset N$ satisfy
$$b^h_{N/E,K}=H_{h,N}(a^X_{N,L,E,K})\,b^h_{N/L,T^X_{L/E}K}\,T^Y_{N/L}(b^h_{L/E,K})\,(a^Y_{N,L,E,H_{h,E}K})^{-1},$$
where in this equation $X=\operatorname{source}(h)$ and $Y=\operatorname{target}(h)$.

Let $d^u_{L/E}:T^{\operatorname{source}(u)}_{L/E}P_{u,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{u,L}T^{\operatorname{target}(u)}_{L/E}$ be the pullback comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and set $U_E=P_{g,E}H_{f,E}$ and $V_E=H_{f',E}P_{g',E}$. Their composite coefficient comparisons are
$$b^U_{L/E,K}=P_{g,L}(b^f_{L/E,K})\,d^g_{L/E,H_{f,E}K},\qquad
b^V_{L/E,K}=H_{f',L}(d^{g'}_{L/E,K})\,b^{f'}_{L/E,P_{g',E}K}.$$
Let $\eta_E:U_E\Rightarrow V_E$ be the rationalization of the specified completed compact-support exchange [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], without any change of its strict-tower normalization. These comparisons intertwine that actual exchange:
$$\eta_{L,T^X_{L/E}K}\,b^U_{L/E,K}=b^V_{L/E,K}\,T^{Y'}_{L/E}(\eta_{E,K}).$$
This statement asserts coefficient coherence, not invertibility of $\eta_E$, and uses neither smoothness nor a base-field hypothesis.

proof.text: Work first with integral ambient derived categories, writing $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$, and $C_W=(-)\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S_W$ is finite free over $R_W$, $C_W$ preserves complete objects, and its specified quotient-tower comparison $\chi$ is the natural isomorphism with the actual integral coefficient extension. Choose an $R_W$-module basis of $S_W$ only for checking isomorphisms at a fixed scheme: it identifies the underlying $R_W$-module functor $C_W$ with a finite biproduct of copies of the identity. Tensor with $S_W$ is therefore exact. All maps below are the canonical balanced maps, independent of this checking basis. The coefficient identifications for scheme inverse image, open restriction and quotient maps are those of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]; its naturality in the inverse system identifies the two coefficient maps in every square. Work at intermediate compactification schemes in ambient categories: no constructibility assertion for an intermediate factor is being assumed.

proof.text: For $k:U\hookrightarrow W$ equal to $j$ or $j'$, construct $\lambda_k:C_Wk_{!,R}\longrightarrow k_{!,S}C_U$. On the direct-sum extension presheaf its formula is $(i_\alpha x)\otimes s\mapsto i_\alpha(x\otimes s)$, where $i_\alpha$ denotes a summand indexed by a map to the open. The inverse of the natural tensor isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], with $\mathcal F=S_W$, is exactly this map after sheafification. It is $S_W$-linear: multiplying $s$ by $s'$ on either side gives $i_\alpha(x\otimes ss')$; balancing over $R_W$ gives the same formula. Thus it is an isomorphism of $S_W$-module sheaves, not merely of underlying $R_W$-modules. Extension by zero is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and tensor with $S_W$ is exact by step 1. Applying the isomorphism degreewise computes both derived functors; [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] supplies the exact derived functors and their shift comparisons. This proves the required derived coefficient-change version without treating the underived tensor lemma itself as a derived or completed assertion.

proof.text: Check the coherence of $\lambda$ on the same summands. For $E\subset L\subset N$ the successive-extension composite sends $((i_\alpha x)\otimes s)\otimes z$ to $i_\alpha(x\otimes sz)$ after the balanced associators; the one-step comparison sends it to precisely that element. These maps respect restrictions and therefore descend to sheafification and complexes. For the repeated field, the tensor unit sends $(i_\alpha x)\otimes1$ to $i_\alpha x$; after the literal identity normalization of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] this is the identity. The maps have degree zero and are degreewise, so commuting them with a cochain shift introduces no sign; their shift square is the one supplied in step 2. This establishes the open-factor unit, successive-field and shift equations, with the specified balanced associators.

proof.text: For every scheme map $q:Z\to W$ used here, use the canonical compatible coefficient identifications from step 1 and apply [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence] to $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ and $S_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,T}$. Step 1 supplies finite freeness; the lemma imposes no dimension or constructibility hypotheses on intermediate schemes. It gives the actual $S_W$-linear counit-tensor comparison $\pi_q:C_WRq_{*,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{*,S}C_Z$, its input-shift square, tensor-unit normalization and successive-coefficient equation. This is the proper direct-image coefficient comparison specified by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], because both are defined by that canonical scalar-extension/projection map. Use this construction for $p,p'$ in the ambient categories.

proof.text: Record carefully how scalar extension interacts with completion units. Let $\Lambda_R,\Lambda_{S,t},\Lambda_{S,v}$ denote the Koszul completion reflectors. The DVR description in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives $t=u v^e$ in $\mathcal O_L$, with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$ (the restricted absolute value gives $0<|t|_L<1$). The local completeness conditions for $(t)$ and $(v)$ in $S_W$ agree: an element of $(t)$ lies in $(v)$, and for any local $a\in(v)$ one has $a^e\in(t)$ and $S_W[1/a]=S_W[1/a^e]$. Hence the Hom-bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] gives a unique unit-preserving natural isomorphism $\Lambda_{S,t}\cong\Lambda_{S,v}$. Tensor with the finite free $S_W$ commutes with the strict Koszul-tower limit: after the basis check in step 1, the comparison with products is the finite-biproduct rearrangement $\bigoplus_{i=1}^d\prod_n^D X_n\cong\prod_n^D\bigoplus_{i=1}^d X_n$; it commutes with $1-s$ and hence with the natural Roos limit triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. At index $n$, tensor sends $[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ to $[S_W\xrightarrow{t^n}S_W]$ and sends the transition $(t,1)$ to $(t,1)$. It therefore gives a unit-preserving isomorphism $C_W\Lambda_R\cong\Lambda_{S,t}C_W\cong\Lambda_{S,v}C_W$. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] the quotient-tower units are these same units. In particular these are comparisons for the actual completed functors, including the specified $\chi$ in step 1, not arbitrary identifications of complete endpoints.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to the open square $(j,j',\bar g',g')$, also on the small ringed diagram sites furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Its derived tensor map gives the reduction comparison $j_!K\otimes_R^L R_n\cong j_!(K\otimes_{R_U}^L R_{n,U})$, with its specified open-unit normalization, for arbitrary complexes. Thus no underived tensor assertion is being substituted for a derived one. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_W$ and $S_n=(\mathcal O_L/t^n)_W$ are exactly the completed-ring quotients. Step 1 reduced modulo $t^n$ makes $S_n$ finite free over $R_n$. The relation $t=uv^e$ of step 5 identifies $S_n$ with $(\mathcal O_L/v^{en})_W$, with its actual quotient maps.

proof.text: In these derived coefficient systems, the open base-change and tensor maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] are characterized by restriction to the identity after the open adjunction units. Their coefficient square therefore commutes: after transposition under the open adjunction, both composites are the same balancing map $x\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes s$. On extension summands this reads $(i_\alpha x)\otimes s\mapsto i_{\alpha'}(g'^*x\otimes s)$ in either order. The normalization lemma applies to the diagram topoi themselves, so this is an equality of derived system morphisms, not an inference from equality of evaluations. Applying the total derived-limit functor preserves that equality. The finite maps are the canonical ones of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], by the last clause of the normalization lemma.

proof.text:
For the $L$ coefficients compare the $v$-quotient tower with its $en$ subsequence by [lem-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction]. Its canonical restriction isomorphism preserves the actual quotient-cone unit and commutes with the strict open/tensor square just proved. Consequently the limit comparison is the unit-preserving comparison of step 5, and the extension-zero/limit maps defining $\beta$ commute with it. This fixes the specified normalization of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] at both fields. Writing $P_u=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and using the canonical completed balancing $d_u$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], the resulting square is
$$(j'_!d_{g'})\lambda_{j',P_{g',R}K}C(\beta_R)=\beta_{S,CK}P_{\bar g',S}(\lambda_{j,K})d_{\bar g',j_!K}.$$
The scalar map is this $d_u$ because the construction preserves both ordinary balancing and its completion unit. For $e=1$ the restriction is literally the identity.

proof.text:
For the proper square $(p,p',g,\bar g')$, cartesian by the construction of $c'$, let $e^R,e^S$ be the ambient mates of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for the coefficient sheaves $R_T$ and $S_T$, identified along the square by step 1, and let $\mu_u:Lu_S^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}CLu_R^*$ be the balancing of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $d_u=\mu_u^{-1}$. First prove in $D(S_{Y'})$ the ambient equation
$e^S_{CM}\,Lg_S^*(\pi_{p,M})\,d_{g,Rp_*M}=Rp'_{*,S}(d_{\bar g',M})\,\pi_{p',L\bar g'^*M}\,C_{Y'}(e^R_M)$.
By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] compare transposes under $Lp'^*_S\dashv Rp'_{*,S}$. The definition in [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence] gives $\varepsilon^S_q\,Lq_S^*\pi_q=C(\varepsilon^R_q)\mu_q$ for $q=p,p'$; the mate definition gives $\varepsilon_{p'}Lp'^*e=L\bar g'^*(\varepsilon_p)\theta$ for both rings. With naturality of $\theta$ and $\mu$, the right side transposes to $d_{\bar g'}C(L\bar g'^*_R\varepsilon^R_p\,\theta^R)\mu_{p'}$ and the left side to $d_{\bar g'}C(L\bar g'^*_R\varepsilon^R_p)\,\mu_{\bar g'}L\bar g'^*_S(\mu_p)\,\theta^S\,Lp'^*_S(d_g)$. On K-flat flat-term representatives $C(\theta^R)\mu_{p'}$ and $\mu_{\bar g'}L\bar g'^*_S(\mu_p)\theta^SLp'^*_S(d_g)$ both send $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes s$ through $p\bar g'=gp'$. So the transposes agree as $S$-module arrows. Pass to completed pullbacks using step 5: precompose with the $S$-completion unit of $C_{Y'}Lg_R^*Rp_{*,R}M$. Step 9 reduces both composites to this ambient equation followed by $Rp'_*$ of the completion unit on the complete target, so the reflector Hom-bijection makes them equal:
$\gamma_{S,C M}\,P_{g,S}(\pi_{p,M})\,d_{g,Rp_*M}=Rp'_{*,S}(d_{\bar g',M})\,\pi_{p',P_{\bar g',R}M}\,C_{Y'}(\gamma_{R,M})$.
Here $d$ on completed pullbacks is the completed balancing of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], the direct-image/limit comparison is that of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]; step 9 fixed $H,H',v_\bullet$.

proof.text: Let $u:T'\to T$ be $g$ or $g'$ and $M\in\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}(T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] (iii), $M$ is bounded, say in cohomological degrees $[a,b]$. The augmented two-term resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{t^n}\mathcal O_E]$ of $\mathcal O_E/t^n$ is [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. The flat constant-to-completed coefficient comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] tensors this to the corresponding resolution over $R_T$. Hence $M_n$ is represented by $M\otimes^L[R_T\xrightarrow{t^n}R_T]$. The cone triangle $M\xrightarrow{t^n}M\to M_n\to M[1]$ gives $\mathcal H^i(M_n)=0$ outside $[a-1,b]$ by its cohomology exact sequence, independently of $n$. This is the common reduction bound required in the next step.

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible] to the cartesian square with vertical maps $\mathrm{id}_T,\mathrm{id}_{T'}$ and both horizontal maps $u$. The four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional, the identities are proper with fibres of dimension at most $0$, and $N=\ell$ annihilates $\mathcal O_E/t$ and is invertible on $T,T'$. The preceding step supplies its common reduction bound. Its stated third conclusion gives $P_uM\in\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}(T')$, with the uniform constructibility and compatible etale-origin witnesses required by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. The square and its pullback comparison are [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Thus this is preservation in the precise completed PBC category, without identifying a different coefficient category with it.

proof.text: On the inherited triangulations of [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], these restricted $P_u$ are exact: [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] writes them as derived reduction tower, derived tower pullback, and total derived limit, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] makes the last functor exact. They are $\mathcal O_E$-linear by [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange], whose domain is the full derived-complete category, so its linearity restricts to this full subcategory. This supplies exactly the hypotheses on $P$ needed for rational transport in the final step. For $f'$ the separated-finite-type hypotheses follow from [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; [def-cbc-compact-support-square] provides the pulled-back compactification. The opens are quasi-compact by [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map].

source.place: Opening scalar-extension paragraph; details supplied by the worker

proof.text: Define $b^h=Rp_{h,*,S}(\lambda_{j_h})\,\pi_{p_h,j_{h,!}(-)}$. The compactification definition [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] says $H_h=Rp_{h,*}j_{h,!}$. Steps 2 and 4 give an exact natural isomorphism. Its endpoints lie in the required integral categories by [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction] for $H_h$ and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] for scalar extension. No separate constructibility claim for the intermediate factors is needed. Compose their unit and shift squares to obtain those for $b^h$. For a tower of fields substitute the successive-field equations for $\lambda$ and $\pi$ into $Rp_*(\lambda)\pi$. Naturality of $\pi$ moves the inner $\lambda$ past $\pi$; the adjacent inverse associators cancel. The surviving factors are $H_{h,N}(a^{\mathrm{source}(h)})$, $b^h_{N/L,C_{L/E}K}$, $C_{N/L}(b^h_{L/E,K})$, $(a^{\mathrm{target}(h)})^{-1}$, in this order. These give exactly the stated $b^h$ equation.

proof.text: Prove the integral compact-support exchange equation by pasting the two established squares. Set $M=j_!K$ and $B=Rp'_*(\beta)\gamma_M$, exactly the ordered composite in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Start with $B_{S,CK}P_{g,S}(b^f)d_{g,H_fK}$. Replace $b^f$ by $Rp_{*,S}(\lambda_j)\pi_p$. Naturality of $\gamma_S$ with respect to $\lambda_j$ changes the initial portion to $Rp'_{*,S}(\beta_{S,CK}P_{\bar g',S}(\lambda_j))\gamma_{S,CM}P_{g,S}(\pi_p)d_g$. Replace the latter three factors using the proper equality of step 10. Inside $Rp'_{*,S}$ the consecutive factors are then $\beta_{S,CK}P_{\bar g',S}(\lambda_j)d_{\bar g',j_!K}$; steps 6–8 replaces them by $(j'_!d_{g'})\lambda_{j',P_{g',R}K}C(\beta_R)$. Naturality of $\pi_{p'}$ moves $C(\beta_R)$ to the right across that projection comparison. The remaining left factors are $H_{f',S}(d_{g'})b^{f'}_{P_{g',R}K}$, and the right factors are $C(Rp'_*(\beta_R)\gamma_{R,j_!K})=C(B_{R,K})$. Therefore $B_{S,CK}b^U=b^V C(B_{R,K})$, with $b^U=P_{g,S}(b^f)d^g$ and $b^V=H_{f',S}(d^{g'})b^{f'}$. This calculation uses no invertibility of $B$ or $\gamma$.

proof.text: Finally localize the integral functors and comparisons. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] there are no new objects: a rational arrow is a finite sum of $u\otimes a$, with integral $u$ and $a\in E$. By [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], the exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear $H,P$ and all their integral natural transformations extend, with component $\eta_K\otimes1$. For the scalar functor the extension on such an arrow is $C(u)\otimes\iota_{L/E}(a)$; this is well defined by balancing, since $C(ru)=\iota(r)C(u)$ and every nonzero $r\in\mathcal O_E$ becomes invertible in $L$. Thus an integral naturality square multiplied by $\iota(a)$ is the required rational naturality square for $u\otimes a$, and additivity handles a general arrow. Apply localization to the equations of steps 3, 4, 14 and 15: it preserves compositions, identities, inverses and shifts. The scalar associators and shifts are those of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], whose integral comparisons were used above. Consequently the rational $b^h$ have the displayed unit, shift and successive-extension laws, their composite comparisons are the stated $b^U,b^V$, and step 15 becomes $\eta_{L,TK}b^U=b^V T(\eta_{E,K})$ for the rationalization of precisely the specified strict-normalized exchange. All hypotheses used were the stated integral-operation domains, finite coefficient extensions and the compactification geometry; no base-field or smoothness assumption was introduced.
